items.title: George Guesnon Interview, 1965-09
items.q: Among them, the well-known and legendary Tomy LaFont. Tomy LaFont. That's right, a plantation owner who left more than a million dollars to charity when he died.

ctx.x: Now, this tape will consist of mostly conversation. George is just going to get his scrapbook. A book where he put all the photographs and written down things in, you know. And he's going to tell me about all of that. Oh!

You see, this is the small part of them that are left. Look at the various colors. See, she's white as your wife is. Sandy, yellow-hand, blue eyes. Yeah, yeah. That's right. Here's another one. You see, well, these are what you call the Creoles of color. Creoles of color. Of New Orleans. Now, listen to this well. You see, before the Civil War, some of the wealthiest citizens of New Orleans were the world-renowned Creoles of color. Of French and Spanish heritage, these great land owners and slaveholders, if they…
They were the most intelligent people.
